title: Your pencils
say: Four pencils today, chosen by value: two-H and H-B for your brightest areas, two-B for the mid-tones, and six-B for your very darkest darks. We'll use all four, one at a time.

title: A tissue for blending
say: You'll also reach for a small tissue later on, to blend your shading smooth. We'll get there in a few steps — for now, just know it's coming.

title: Feel your paper
hint: A little tooth helps the pencil grip.
say: Feel your own paper before you start. A little tooth helps the pencil grip — that's what gives foil its soft, believable shine.

title: Where your balloon will sit
say: Before the first line — leave space around your balloon. It sits slightly off-centre, a little tilted, so check the size before any detail. Lightly mark where your balloon will sit. I'll wait.

title: Find the tilt before the outline
watchSay: Watch for the tilt — the teacher's first lines aren't straight up and down. They lean, just slightly, crossing near the middle.
say: Now your turn — lightly cross two tilted guide lines near your centre mark. Take your time. I'll wait.

card.title: Find the tilt before the outline
card.sub: Compare the guide lines before adding detail.

title: Block in the whole shape first
watchSay: Keep going all the way around — block in the whole star before fixing any single point. Size first, detail later.
say: Rough in all six points lightly, all the way around. Don't worry about perfect symmetry yet. I'll wait.

card.title: Block in the whole shape first
card.sub: Size and placement matter before any detail.

title: Turn corners into soft curves
watchSay: Watch the teacher keep adjusting the edges — drawing, checking, and redrawing until the shape feels right. Even teachers correct their lines. That's how a good shape is found.
say: Your turn. Soften each corner into a gentle curve. If a line looks wrong, just adjust it — the teacher does too. I'll wait.

card.title: Turn corners into soft curves
card.sub: Foil has volume: let the edges bend.

title: Clean up with a light touch
watchSay: The teacher keeps refining this pass — a light touch, going back over a line that still needs adjusting before it's final.
say: Keep refining your own lines too, with a light touch. Nothing needs to be perfect yet. I'll wait.

card.title: Clean up with a light touch
card.sub: A light touch while the shape still settles.

title: Erasing the guide lines
watchSay: Now the teacher erases the guide lines. They helped us find the tilt and the shape at the start. The outline is set now, so we don't need them anymore.
say: Gently erase your guide lines too, and keep your outline. Take your time.

card.title: Erasing the guide lines
card.sub: The tilt lines did their job — now let them go.

title: Separate the seam from the outline
watchSay: Look closely at the rim just inside the outline — that seam is separate from the outer edge, and it matters.
say: Add a thin line just inside your outline, like a seam. Keep that narrow gap visible. I'll wait.

card.title: Separate the seam from the outline
card.sub: Look for the narrow rim inside the edge.

title: Let folds turn toward the centre
watchSay: These small curves are folds in the foil. Notice how they turn from the rim toward the centre, not straight across.
say: Add a few light fold lines, curving in toward the middle. Just a few is enough. I'll wait.

card.title: Let folds turn toward the centre
card.sub: Follow each fold's direction.

title: Your outline is ready
watchSay: A few more fold marks, and the outline is complete — a strong shape with soft edges, ready for shading.
say: Take one more look at your whole outline before we bring in the light and dark. I'll wait.

card.title: Strong shape, soft edges
card.sub: Ready for light and dark.

title: Outline complete
hint: Your outline is ready — next time, we bring in the light and dark.
say: Your outline is ready. That's the hardest part done — next time, we bring in the light and dark.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Look closely at the edge
watchSay: In the outline, straight lines helped us find the big shape fast. Now the teacher slows down and looks closely at the edge. Still life is all about detail — every bump and dent in the foil is worth seeing.
say: Look at the reference. Find one edge that isn't straight. Take your time.

card.title: Look closely at the edge
card.sub: A straight guess, next to what's really there.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Move point to point
watchSay: The teacher follows the outer edge one point at a time. Where the foil bulges, the line bulges. Where it dents, the line dips in. Once it matches what's really there, it gets darker.
say: Pick one point. Follow its edge slowly — look, then draw the bumps you see. Darken it only once you're sure.

card.title: Move point to point
card.sub: One point at a time, all the way around.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Light side, shadow side
watchSay: The light here comes from the upper left, so each point has a light side and a shadow side. Once an edge is confirmed, it's mostly the shadow side that gets darker.
say: Find your own light direction, then look closely at each edge before you darken it — mostly on the shadow side. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Light side, shadow side
card.sub: Light from the upper left — confirmed edges darken on the shadow side.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: A quick clean-up, then keep going
watchSay: Here the teacher lightens a line that didn't match, and looks again. Observing means checking and correcting.
say: If an edge doesn't match what you see, lighten it and look again. There's no rush.

card.title: A quick clean-up, then keep going
card.sub: Check against what you see, then correct.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Leave the paper white here
watchSay: Notice what's happening inside each point — nothing, not yet. Right now only the edge is being refined. That white paper stays white, and later it becomes the bright shine of the foil.
say: Keep the inside of each shape empty for now — just refine the edge. Leave the paper white there. I'll wait.

card.title: Leave the paper white here
card.sub: Only the edge is being refined — this stays white.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Take a breath and compare
watchSay: The teacher stops and looks — hands off the page, comparing the drawing against the real foil edge. Checking is part of observing, not just the drawing itself.
say: Hold your drawing at arm's length and compare it with the reference. Are any edges still too smooth or too straight? Foil edges wave.

card.title: Take a breath and compare
card.sub: Check your edges against the reference.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Edges confirmed
watchSay: A few more edges checked and confirmed, and the whole outline now matches what the teacher really sees — ready for tone.
say: Take one more look at your whole star — every edge checked against what you see. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Every edge checked against reality
card.sub: Ready for tone.

chapter: Light and Dark on the Structure
title: Light and dark complete
hint: Your edges now follow what you really see — next, we build the tone across the whole form.
say: Your edges now follow what you really see. That's real observation. Next, we build the tone across the whole form.

title: Stroke direction follows the form
watchSay: Watch the direction of these strokes — they follow the curve of each puffed section, not a flat grid. Tone that follows the form is what makes it look round, not flat.
say: Choose one section of your own star. Stroke in the direction that section curves, not straight up and down. Take your time.

card.title: Stroke direction follows the form
card.sub: Strokes run with the curve, not against it.

title: Keep following each curve
watchSay: Same idea, a new section — the stroke direction changes because the curve changes.
say: Move to another section. Let your strokes follow that section's own curve. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Keep following each curve
card.sub: A different section, a different direction.

title: Build it gradually
watchSay: Notice the tone builds in thin layers, not one heavy pass — the teacher goes over the same area more than once, always following the same curve.
say: Build your own tone the same way: light layers, more than one pass, rather than pressing hard once. Take it slowly.

card.title: Build it gradually
card.sub: Thin layers, more than one pass.

title: Another section, same patience
watchSay: Now another section gets the same gradual build-up, strokes still following its curve.
say: Pick another section and keep layering lightly, following its curve. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Another section, same patience
card.sub: Still light layers, still following the curve.

title: Still the same pencil
watchSay: Still the same HB — the deeper tone comes from more layers, not a softer pencil.
say: Keep building with your own HB. Add another layer wherever it still looks too light. I'll wait.

card.title: Still the same pencil
card.sub: More layers, not a softer pencil.

title: Keep the whole star moving together
watchSay: The teacher doesn't finish one point before starting the next — tone builds across the whole star together.
say: Don't chase one perfect section — add a little tone to several areas, then come back. Take your time.

card.title: Keep the whole star moving together
card.sub: A little tone everywhere, not one point finished.

title: Protect each highlight
watchSay: Look closely — it's not just one bright spot. Each puffed section keeps its own highlight, left white while the tone around it deepens.
say: Find each section's own brightest spot and leave it alone, even as you darken what's around it. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Protect each highlight
card.sub: Every section keeps its own bright spot.

title: Deepen the darks near each highlight
watchSay: Right next to each protected highlight, the tone jumps noticeably darker — the dark sits right next to the light, patch by patch, not a smooth fade. That's real contrast already; the darkest, crispest accents still come later, with a 6B pencil.
say: Push the tone darker right beside your own protected highlights. The bigger the jump, the brighter they'll read. There's no rush.

card.title: Deepen the darks near each highlight
card.sub: Dark next to light, patch by patch.

title: Last layers across the form
watchSay: A final round across the whole star — connecting the tones and filling any area that's still too pale. The contrast stays.
say: Take one more pass. Fill the areas that still look thin, but keep your highlights white and your darks strong.

card.title: Last layers across the form
card.sub: Connect the tones — keep the contrast.

title: Ready for the tissue
watchSay: Tone is built across the whole form now, with each highlight protected — next, a tissue will blend it smooth.
say: Take one more look at your whole star before we blend it smooth. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: Every highlight protected
card.sub: Ready for the tissue.

title: Tone complete
hint: Tone is built across the whole form — next, we blend it smooth with a tissue.
say: Tone is built across the whole star, with every highlight protected. That's real patience. Next, we blend it smooth with a tissue.

title: A clean corner, light pressure
watchSay: The teacher folds the tissue to a clean corner, and blends along the form — never in circles — with a light touch.
say: Fold your tissue to a clean corner and blend one area along the form. Light pressure. Take your time.

card.title: A clean corner, light pressure
card.sub: Blend along the form, not in circles.

title: Keep the highlight clean
watchSay: Close to the highlight — but never across it. Then the next area.
say: Blend each area the same way, right up to the highlight, never over it. Do the whole star. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Keep the highlight clean
card.sub: Every highlight stays protected, area by area.

title: Before and after
watchSay: Softer — but the contrast is still there. Smooth, not flat.
say: Compare your drawing with before. If a highlight turned grey, press a kneaded eraser on it gently to lift it back. Tap Continue when you're ready.

title: Blending complete
hint: Your tone is smooth, and the contrast is still there — next, we add the darkest details.
say: Your tone is smooth, and the contrast is still there. That's the balance foil needs. Next, we add the darkest details.
